text:
carla: FYI I opened a PR to clean up several console + observability docs issues we hit in a recent support case: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/3124 — summary in the PR description. can folks help review today? :wave:

matt: link? I'll take a look after standup. quick TL;DR here in the thread please.

carla: TL;DR of the fixes: 
- unify trace header to `x-rd-trace` across Go/Rust/Python examples (some pages still had `Trace-Id` or `X-Trace-Id`)
- update Go/Rust snippet fields: `resp.CostTokens` -> `resp.Usage["tokens"]` and `usage.tokens` respectively
- dashboard preset example had `sampling: auto` and `percentile_name: p95` (stale) — renamed to `sampling_strategy: percentile` + `metric_percentile: p99` to match the dashboard UI
- corrected cost/latency numbers in the quickstart cost table after batching-defaults change, added a 1-line note about ~6% delta
- removed an orphan `kv_prefetch` flag from a couple of YAML examples that confused customers
- added a tiny nginx proxy snippet showing header passthrough and a curl debug example

zhao: awesome. can we also add a tiny QA test in docs-examples CI that runs the quickstart snippet and asserts the example contains `x-rd-trace` and `usage` keys? would catch regressions early. I can draft that test if we agree on the assertion.

eli: pinging runtime folks: do we have any plans to accept older header names at the ingress layer? if not, we should be strict in docs and add compatibility notes for Dedicated customers who pin older SDKs.

carla: runtime confirmed offline that they won't be normalizing legacy header names; added a compatibility note in the PR: "If you run SDK/runtime <2.5, telemetry field names may differ; see migration guide." linked to /sdk/migration/telemetry-headers.

docs-bot: linkcheck: build failed: 1 broken anchor in /sdk/migration/telemetry-headers.md line 12 -> /sdk/migration/telemetry-headers#legacy-names (404). Suggested fix: remove anchor or point to /sdk/migration/telemetry-headers#legacy-field-mapping.

matt: thanks docs-bot. carla, please fix the anchor in the migration doc or update the link target. also update the Go snippet to show the minimal example users will copy: 
```go
// after a generation request
if tokens, ok := resp.Usage["tokens"]; ok {
  fmt.Println("tokens:", tokens)
}
```
and add the curl check: `curl -H 'x-rd-trace: dbg-123' https://app.example/ping -v` and expected `x-rd-trace: dbg-123` in response headers.

zhao: I'll open the site-config redirect PR once we decide the canonical migration URL to avoid CI linkcheck noise.

eli: small docs UX ask: for the cost table change, add a short changelog line and a one-sentence explanation of why numbers shifted (batching defaults), so customers don't think we silently changed billing.

carla: added a short changelog entry and the batching explanation. updated the migration link to the correct anchor per docs-bot suggestion. pushed fixup.

matt: leaving two nits (wording + inline code fence style) and then LGTM. can we squat the examples so they remain copy-paste safe for Dedicated customers (i.e., avoid config keys that only exist in cloud-hosted consoles)?

carla: good point — I moved the advanced dashboard preset into a "note" box and left the minimal, copy-pasteable YAML at the top. also added a one-line callout for Dedicated: "If you import presets into Dedicated, verify namespaced metric keys to avoid collisions."

zhao: site-config PR opened for a redirect: https://github.com/redwood-inference/site-config/pull/455 — 301 from the old anchor to /sdk/migration/telemetry-headers#legacy-field-mapping. will follow up with infra review.

docs-bot: CI: docs build currently failing on main due to earlier broken anchor. once site-config redirect merges and docs are updated the linkcheck should be green.

eli: great. once CI + redirect are green, can someone squash the tiny commits and merge? i'll help verify runtime telemetry mapping after the docs land.

carla: will squash & merge after docs CI green and the redirect PR is approved. thanks for the quick reviews everyone :rocket:
